K4.claim: pos_at_vcol, which the contract lists "for j/k goals", lands on a tab or wide character that spans the goal column. layout.rs:474-479 returns the last stop with vcol ≤ goal, over the whole display line. Scratch: TextBuf::new("a\tb\n").pos_at_vcol(0, 3) = 1, the tab; move-to-column 3 lands on b, at 2.

Contract §9:252: "pos_at_vcol: the position at a display column, for j/k goals".

verifier.reasoning:
Scratch: on `a\tb\n`, pos_at_vcol(0,v) is 1 (the tab) for v = 1..7, and 2 only at v = 8. On `a中b`, vcol 2 gives 1 (the wide character).

The user's Evil (verify-text-and-keys/evil/jk.el):

- `j` from col 2 onto `a中bc` lands on b at col 3.

So Evil lands after a character that spans the goal column. die-vim's pos_at_col (die-vim/src/text.rs:149-160) reimplements this and doesn't call core. It's used at motions.rs:127 and insert.rs:217.

The proposed fix is flawed:

K9.claim: The Scene holds core's pointer map (`positions`) and no row revision. K9's `handle(pointer)` needs that map after the frame is handed to die-render, and R2's diff wants to keep the previous frame. Neither works until `scene()`'s ownership is decided, and R2's test plan (the frame-data boundary) is written against whatever is decided now.
K9.proposed_fix:
Recommended:
1. K9's `pub fn scene(&mut self) -> Scene`, documented as: "A fresh frame, owned by the caller. die-render keeps the previous one and rebuilds only the rows whose cells differ, so core keeps no render state."
2. Move `positions` out of Scene into a Ctx field that compose fills, exposed as `pub fn position_at(&self, row: usize, col: usize) -> Option<(WindowId, usize)>`. It means "the window and buffer position the cell at (row, col) showed in the last composed frame". K9's handle(pointer), the harness and K8's two position tests use it. Scene becomes drawing-only.
3. R2's test plan:
   - `only_changed_rows_are_rebuilt` compares `prev.row(r) != next.row(r)`.
   - `scrolling_one_line_rebuilds_one_row` matches the new row r against the previous row r±1, by comparison and not SipHash.
Alternative, if preferred: Ctx owns the Scene and reuses its buffers, `scene(&mut self) -> &Scene`, and `put` compares before writing and bumps `row_rev: Vec<u64>`. That's about 20 more lines in core, with positions kept in the Scene.
K9.recommendation: The owned Scene, with positions in Ctx: it matches platforms.md's split, and the measured diff cost is negligible.

verifier.reasoning: `positions` is in Scene (scene.rs:147-151), and compose allocates a fresh Scene on every call (scene.rs:285-292). I measured size_of Option<(WindowId, usize)> = 16 and Cell = 40. platforms.md §5.2 (line 241) puts 'Scene diff, row cache' in die-render. The M0 log already deferred K8-7 (pointer mapping) to K9, so the question is open, and K9 and R2 both start in phase 1. Nothing outside die-core reads `positions` today, so moving it now costs only K8's two position tests (positions_map_cells_to_buffer_positions and every_cell_of_a_tab_or_wide_character_maps_to_its_position). Moving it after K7, K9 or K14 adopt it would break their callers. That justifies 'major' under the API-shape rule, though nothing misbehaves today. One part of the claim is overstated: K9 could still work with positions in the Scene (take or clone them before handing the Scene over), so this is a design choice, not a blocker.
verifier.decision_view:
Move positions to Ctx and make Scene drawing-only, as the reviewer recommends. My reasons:
1. Core answering clicks from the map of the frame it last composed is what Emacs does: posn-at-x-y reads the last redisplay's glyph matrix.
2. The diff belongs in die-render (platforms.md §5.2), and it needs only cells.
3. Positions are core semantics that die-render has no use for.
4. Headless tests (K7) and K14 use `ctx.position_at(row, col)` without a renderer.

Decide it in K9's API diff, and write R2's tests as `prev.row(r) != next.row(r)`. Skip the row_rev alternative: it puts render state into core, and the measured diff (about 0.07 ms per frame) doesn't need it.

V3/V4.claim: Because register text is parsed as notation, `@` on a register that `q` didn't record fails on yanked Rust code, or presses keys named in it. Vim and Evil type it literally.
V3/V4.proposed_fix:
Contract §7 sentence: "A register that `q` recorded holds notation; any other register holds plain text, and `@` types it as it is, one key per character, as Vim and Evil do."

Core:
```rust
/// `text` as notation that types it literally: `<` becomes `<lt>`.
pub fn escape_notation(text: &str) -> String { text.replace('<', "<lt>") }
```
The Register type gets `pub keys: bool`, set by `q`. die-vim's `@` feeds `escape_notation(text)` when it's false.

Trade-off: a recorded macro that's pasted, edited and yanked back becomes plain text.
V3/V4.recommendation: Adopt. Running yanked text matters more than editing macros as text.

verifier.decision_view:
Adopt.
- `"ayy` then `@a` on a line of commands is a common Vim idiom, and code full of `<` must not error or press keys named in it.
- The cost is the trade-off the reviewer named: a recorded macro that's pasted, edited and yanked back becomes plain text. It can be re-recorded with `q`.

V3/V4.claim: Selection can't say "each line to its end" for V4's `<C-v>$`. The scene's block highlight also misses a tab or wide character that starts left of the block.
V3/V4.evidence:
text.rs:68 says of goal: "die-vim decides what it means".

scene.rs:527-530 builds the block from display_col(anchor) to display_col(head), and tests each cell's start column only.
V3/V4.proposed_fix:
Selection rustdoc: "On a `Block` selection, `goal == Some(usize::MAX)` means each line to its end, as `$` in Vim's visual block."

scene.rs: when that holds, the column range ends at usize::MAX. Highlight a cell when its item's columns overlap the block's (start ≤ right && end > left).

verifier.reasoning:
- Selection.goal's doc says "die-vim decides what it means" (text.rs:68).
- The scene builds a block from display_col(anchor) to display_col(head) and tests only each cell's start column (`vcols.contains(&t.display_col(q))` in draw_text's style_at). It never reads goal, so `<C-v>$` can't be drawn.
- A tab or wide character that starts left of the block's left column but covers it isn't highlighted.
- The usize::MAX sentinel mirrors Vim's curswant = MAXCOL and Evil's most-positive-fixnum goal. With it, die-vim's pos_at_col naturally lands on each line's end.
- The overlap test is right if the item's end is exclusive (start + width).

V5.claim: Pattern exposes no captures, so V5's `:s` with `$1` would need a second regex engine in die-vim, with its own syntax settings.

search.rs:17-47: the Regex is private, and only search, matches and match_at use it.

scope.md:351 calls for `:s` with Rust regex, keeping case.

```rust
/// Each match in `range`, in order and without overlaps, with `template` expanded (`$1`, `${name}`, `$$`, as regex's `Captures::expand` does): what `:s` replaces.
pub fn replacements(&self, t: &TextBuf, range: Range<usize>, template: &str) -> Vec<(Range<usize>, String)>
```
Built on regex-automata's `Regex::search_captures` and `util::interpolate::string`. Keeping case stays in die-vim.

- Pattern's Regex is private (search.rs:17-21), and only search, matches and match_at use it.
- Pattern::new sets multi_line(true) and crlf(true) (search.rs:26-29). die-vim would have to copy those settings to compile its own captures regex, and the two would drift.
- scope §10 requires `:s`.
- The proposed `replacements` built on regex-automata's search_captures and util::interpolate::string exists in the pinned regex-automata 0.4.18.
- Leaving case preservation to die-vim is right.
